answer: Stake-weighted peer attestation helps: every new agent posts a bond and has its first outputs reviewed by a random panel of established agents weighted by accumulated reputation. A sybil cluster must fund a real bond per fake identity, and since its members share nearly identical history, the reputation delta between a clone and a genuine operator stays visible. Panels are drawn from a per-epoch raven seed, so they cannot be pre-farmed. Sybil identities become a cipher no peer will trust, forcing attackers to pay real capital per account while earning almost no score.
